title: Despite fanfare, Xi shows Trump no sign of breaking with Iran
gist: The Xi-Trump summit produced no tangible Chinese commitment on Iran; China remains Iran's economic and diplomatic lifeline, buying 90%+ of its oil exports (534k bpd in August vs ~1.4m bpd in 2025), vetoing a UN sanctions-panel extension and keeping air links open. Experts argue China's support runs through private teapots and third-party networks, giving Xi plausible deniability and making any deal hard to enforce.

insights.claim: China buys upward of 90% of Iran's exported oil, often at steep discounts, making it essential to keeping the Iranian regime afloat.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
entities: US-China Economic and Security Review Commission
insights.so_what: Chinese demand is the key swing factor in Iran's ability to withstand US pressure.
insights.quote: China is essentially key to keeping the Iranian regime afloat at the moment,

insights.claim: Chinese imports of Iranian oil averaged 534,000 bpd in August versus roughly 1.4 million bpd in 2025, per Kpler, meaning flows fell during the war but did not stop.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Roughly a 60% drop in Iranian flows to China quantifies the war's supply impact and residual sanctions leakage.
insights.quote: Chinese imports averaged 534,000 barrels per day in August, compared with roughly 1.4 million bpd in 2025

insights.claim: Iran's 2025 oil exports to China were worth around $31.2 billion.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Sizes the economic stake for both sides in maintaining the trade.

insights.claim: China and Russia vetoed a US-drafted UNSC resolution extending the Iran sanctions experts panel, ending its mandate though the underlying sanctions remain.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Weaker multilateral monitoring eases sanctions evasion.

insights.claim: China has kept air links with Iran open despite new US aviation sanctions, with a Mahan Air flight landing in Guangzhou, as other countries cut connections.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: China defying new sanctions signals limited willingness to cooperate with US pressure.

themes.theme: Limits of US leverage on Beijing

insights.claim: Historically Beijing rarely uses its regional leverage for reasons that do not directly benefit China, so any Trump commitment from Xi is likely a half-measure at best.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Do not price a Chinese-brokered Iran settlement; China's oil interest outweighs US asks.
insights.quote: Any commitment Trump gets from Xi during this summit is likely to be a half-measure on the ground, at best.

insights.claim: China's support to Iran flows through private teapot refineries and third-party entities, giving Xi plausible deniability to claim the state has stopped while dual-use support continues.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Sanctions targeting will likely focus on teapots and intermediaries, creating idiosyncratic risk for Chinese independent refiners.
insights.quote: The very nature of China’s support to Iran allows Xi some wiggle room in the form of plausible deniability,

insights.claim: Chinese entities sent roughly 1,300 shipments of dual-use components to Iran's Defense Ministry in the first half of 2026, including electronics usable in drones and missile guidance, per the WSJ.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Raises odds of US secondary sanctions on Chinese electronics/components suppliers.

insights.claim: Supporting Iran gives China a low-cost way to back a partner that complicates US military operations without a formal defence commitment.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Structural incentive for China to sustain Iran makes the conflict longer-lived.
insights.quote: a relatively low-cost way to support a partner capable of complicating US military operations

insights.claim: Even if Trump secured a private commitment from Xi, the mix of state policy, private companies and third-party networks would make any agreement difficult to enforce.
insights.speaker: Rosaleen Carroll
insights.so_what: Any announced US-China Iran understanding should be discounted.
